vocabulary.definition: One of the four parts of a coordinate grid, numbered I to IV.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Captain Vega’s Treasure Square
revealWordProblem.text: Captain Vega buried treasure at the four corners of a square. Three corners are at (2, 2), (2, 6), and (6, 6). She always plots her corners in Quadrant I. What ordered pair is the fourth corner, and what is the side length of the square?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A blank coordinate plane with x- and y-axes and a grid, for plotting points.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The fourth corner is (6, 2). The square has a side length of 4 units, because from (2, 2) to (6, 2) is 6 − 2 = 4 units and from (2, 2) to (2, 6) is 6 − 2 = 4 units.

questions.stem: Which ordered pair names a point 3 units right and 7 units up from the origin?
questions.explanation: The first coordinate is horizontal (right 3), the second is vertical (up 7). So (3, 7).
choiceFeedback: You swapped the x and y—the first number is horizontal, second is vertical.
Remember the x-coordinate tells you how far horizontally.
The first number is the horizontal (right/left) distance.
hints: Re-read the moves: 3 units right, then 7 units up. Which move comes first in an ordered pair?
An ordered pair is (x, y): x is the right/left distance, y is the up/down distance. Match each move to its slot.
Start at the origin and go right 3 — that 3 is the x, the first number. Now decide where the 'up 7' goes.
questions.stemEs: ¿Qué par ordenado nombra un punto que está 3 unidades a la derecha y 7 unidades hacia arriba desde el origen?
questions.explanationEs: La primera coordenada es horizontal (3 a la derecha) y la segunda es vertical (7 hacia arriba). Entonces (3, 7).
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer los movimientos: 3 unidades a la derecha y luego 7 unidades hacia arriba. ¿Cuál movimiento va primero en un par ordenado?
Un par ordenado es (x, y): x es la distancia derecha/izquierda y y es la distancia arriba/abajo. Une cada movimiento con su lugar.
Empieza en el origen y ve 3 a la derecha: ese 3 es la x, el primer número. Ahora decide dónde va el 'arriba 7'.

questions.stem: What are the coordinates of the origin?
questions.explanation: The origin is where the x-axis and y-axis cross, at (0, 0).
choiceFeedback: The origin is where both axes cross, where both values are zero.
Both coordinates at the origin are 0 — not mixed with 1.
The origin is where the two axes cross each other. At that crossing point, how far along is each axis? That tells you both coordinates.
hints: The origin is the exact spot where the x-axis and y-axis cross. Picture that crossing point.
Ask: how far right have you moved at the origin? How far up? Those two distances are the coordinates.
At the crossing point you haven't moved right at all, so x = 0. Now figure out the y-value the same way.
questions.explanationEs: El origen es donde se cruzan el eje x y el eje y, en (0, 0).
hintsEs: El origen es el punto exacto donde se cruzan el eje x y el eje y. Imagina ese cruce.
Pregunta: en el origen, ¿cuánto te has movido a la derecha? ¿Y hacia arriba? Esas dos distancias son las coordenadas.
En el punto de cruce no te has movido nada a la derecha, así que x = 0. Ahora halla el valor de y igual.

questions.stem: A point is at (6, 2). What does the 6 tell you?
questions.explanation: The first number (x-coordinate) tells you horizontal movement. 6 means go right 6 units from the origin.
choiceFeedback: The first number controls horizontal movement—check which number moves you up.
With a positive first number, you move right—not left.
Not quite. The first number (x-coordinate) tells you horizontal movement.
hints: In (6, 2), the 6 is the FIRST number. First and second positions have different jobs.
First number = x = horizontal (right/left). Second number = y = vertical (up/down). Positive means right or up.
The 6 sits in the x spot and it's positive, so it describes a horizontal move. Which direction is positive x?
questions.stemEs: Un punto está en (6, 2). ¿Qué te indica el 6?
questions.explanationEs: El primer número (la coordenada x) indica el movimiento horizontal. El 6 significa avanzar 6 unidades a la derecha desde el origen.
choicesEs: El punto está en el cuadrante 6
hintsEs: En (6, 2), el 6 es el PRIMER número. La primera y la segunda posición tienen trabajos distintos.
Primer número = x = horizontal (derecha/izquierda). Segundo número = y = vertical (arriba/abajo). Positivo significa derecha o arriba.
El 6 está en el lugar de x y es positivo, así que describe un movimiento horizontal. ¿Qué dirección es x positiva?

reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Graph on the Coordinate Plane is swapping the order of the coordinates — moving up/down first instead of right/left first. For example, when plotting (5, 2), students often move up 5 and right 2, landing on the wrong point (2, 5) instead of (5, 2). Remember: the x-coordinate (first number) always tells you how far to move right or left along the x-axis; the y-coordinate (second number) tells you how far up or down along the y-axis.

level2.prompt: A student says that (3, 5) and (5, 3) are the same point because they use the same numbers. Is the student correct? Explain why or why not, and describe where each point is located on the coordinate plane.
level2.sentenceFrame: The student is ___ because (3, 5) means ___ while (5, 3) means ___. The ORDER matters because ___.
level2.hint: Compare what each coordinate pair tells you about horizontal and vertical moves.
hints: Both pairs use 3 and 5, but look at which number sits in the x (first) spot in each pair.
Describe each point's moves separately: (3, 5) = right ?, up ?; (5, 3) = right ?, up ?. Compare the two paths.
First step: for (3, 5), go right 3 and up 5. Now do (5, 3)'s moves and check whether you land on the same dot.
level2.explanation: The student is not correct. In (3, 5) the 3 is the x-coordinate, so you move right 3 and up 5, landing high and toward the left. In (5, 3) the 5 is the x-coordinate, so you move right 5 and up 3, landing lower and farther right. Same digits, different jobs — the order inside an ordered pair decides which direction each number controls.
level2.explanationEs: El estudiante no tiene razón. En (3, 5) el 3 es la coordenada x, así que te mueves 3 a la derecha y 5 hacia arriba, y caes alto y hacia la izquierda. En (5, 3) el 5 es la coordenada x, así que te mueves 5 a la derecha y 3 hacia arriba, y caes más abajo y más a la derecha. Los mismos dígitos, distintas funciones: el orden dentro del par ordenado decide qué dirección controla cada número.
level2.promptEs: Un estudiante dice que (3, 5) y (5, 3) son el mismo punto porque usan los mismos números. ¿Tiene razón? Explica por qué sí o por qué no y describe dónde se ubica cada punto en el plano de coordenadas.
hintsEs: Ambos pares usan 3 y 5, pero fíjate en qué número está en el lugar de x (el primero) en cada par.
Describe los movimientos de cada punto por separado: (3, 5) = derecha ?, arriba ?; (5, 3) = derecha ?, arriba ?. Compara las dos rutas.
Primer paso: para (3, 5), ve 3 a la derecha y 5 hacia arriba. Ahora haz los movimientos de (5, 3) y revisa si caes en el mismo punto.

level3.stem: Starting at the origin, which point is located by moving 4 units LEFT and 3 units UP?
choiceFeedback: Moving LEFT makes x negative. Four units left of the origin gives x = negative 4.
The coordinates are swapped and the signs with them. The x-coordinate comes first.
The two numbers are swapped. Four left gives x = negative 4 and three up gives y = 3.
level3.explanation: An ordered pair is (x, y). Moving left makes x negative, so x = −4; moving up makes y positive, so y = 3. The point is (−4, 3).
